column3: A faction's calculated display of belief and later rejection offers a broad parallel to deceptive withdrawal.
Fearful flight is later reframed as part of a return to commissioned responsibility.
Its warning against harmful division and claims of effect apart from permission only broadly frames false control.
Those satisfied with staying behind cannot later recast a request to join as trustworthy commitment.

It denies that anyone can shield them from God's intended harm or mercy, challenging security sought through retreat.
It exposes those who hinder others and summon their brothers away while offering only meager participation in battle.
It portrays their fear, self-protective speech, and expectation that the confederates will return, completing the focus's diagnosis.
